meta.title: From active dendrites to causal circuit interfaces
meta.thesis: Across this five-year window, the clearest lab-level progression is from asking how dendrites can support nonlinear learning, to identifying a natural use of active dendrites in cortical feedback, and then to building increasingly precise tools for reading and perturbing neural computation during behavior. Cerebellar learning and International Brain Laboratory work extend the scale, but remain distinct branches rather than evidence for one universal mechanism.
meta.boundary: This is a selected claim map, not a complete bibliography. Lab-led experiments, reviews, methods papers and large collaborations are separated. Co-authorship is not treated as proof that every consortium result belongs to the Häusser lab's central program.
meta.affiliation: Professor of Neuroscience and Director, School of Biomedical Sciences, The University of Hong Kong; Honorary Professor in Neural Computation, UCL

streams.label: Dendrites and feedback
streams.question: How can dendrites learn and integrate distributed inputs that are not reducible to a point neuron?
streams.synthesis: The strongest bridge runs from a local learning-rule existence result to direct evidence that apical dendrites nonlinearly integrate spatially offset cortical feedback.

streams.label: Cortical causality
streams.question: When does activity in a defined cortical ensemble causally change a perceptual decision?
streams.synthesis: Perturbation effects are conditional: cell identity, sensory contrast, inhibitory routing and behavioral engagement jointly determine whether activation helps, harms or does nothing.

streams.label: All-optical interfaces
streams.short: Read, write and close the loop
streams.question: How can experiments target the right cells or branches at the right moment while behavior unfolds?
streams.synthesis: The tool chain advances from a reproducible read-write protocol to online closed-loop perturbation, subthreshold voltage readout and computational correction of off-target stimulation.

streams.label: Cerebellar learning
streams.question: How are instructive signals and plasticity organized across cerebellar circuits and learning timescales?
streams.synthesis: A review-level reward framework is followed by tools and experiments that resolve cell types, synaptic plasticity and distinct fast and slow climbing-fiber learning signals.

streams.label: Brain-wide collaboration
streams.question: How can local circuit questions be embedded in reproducible, distributed measurements across the brain?
streams.synthesis: IBL and Neuropixels collaborations provide shared infrastructure and brain-wide maps. They broaden measurement scale, but do not by themselves establish a dendritic explanation for distributed decision variables.

questions.label: How do dendrites learn and integrate nonlinear input?
When does a cortical ensemble causally alter perception?
How can neural activity be read and written in closed loop?
How are cerebellar teaching signals split across timescales?
How can local computation be measured at brain-wide scale?

syntheses.label: Dendrites are a learnable and experimentally observed nonlinear substrate, not a universal explanation.
Causal effects depend on ensemble identity, inhibition, stimulus strength and engagement.
Measurement is moving from population calcium signals toward online and subthreshold control.
Cerebellar learning signals are heterogeneous across source, target and timescale.
Shared standards and high-density probes make distributed claims testable across laboratories.

records.title: A synaptic learning rule for exploiting nonlinear dendritic computation
records.claim: A local, voltage-dependent supervised learning rule can adjust synapses in a detailed pyramidal neuron model so that the neuron exploits nonlinear interactions across its dendritic tree.
records.evidence: The rule was derived and tested in a morphologically detailed model with active dendrites. Local pre- and postsynaptic signals captured interactions that a point-neuron update would miss.
records.boundary: This is a computational existence and performance result. It does not show that biological synapses implement this exact rule, or that active dendrites are necessary for every learning task.
records.contribution: Turns dendritic nonlinearity from an anatomical complication into a trainable computational resource.

records.title: Reward signals in the cerebellum: Origins, targets, and functional implications
records.claim: Reward expectation, delivery, size and omission are represented in cerebellar pathways, motivating models that combine supervised and reinforcement-like learning.
records.evidence: The paper synthesizes evidence for reward-related mossy- and climbing-fiber signals and discusses how their convergence could drive Purkinje-cell plasticity.
records.boundary: This is a review and conceptual framework, not a new causal experiment demonstrating one unified cerebellar reward algorithm.
records.contribution: Defines the cerebellar branch's central question before later work resolves cells, synapses and timescales.

records.title: All-optical interrogation of neural circuits in behaving mice
records.claim: Two-photon calcium imaging and holographic optogenetics can be combined into a reproducible workflow for cellular-resolution read-write experiments in awake mice.
records.evidence: The protocol covers preparation, calibration, targeting and analysis, with demonstrations in barrel cortex, visual cortex and hippocampus.
records.boundary: A protocol establishes technical feasibility and reproducibility. It does not by itself establish a biological mechanism or guarantee artifact-free causal interpretation.
records.contribution: Creates the experimental base used by the later perception and closed-loop studies.

records.title: Behaviorally relevant decision coding in primary somatosensory cortex neurons
records.claim: A subset of layer 2/3 somatosensory neurons carries decision-related activity that can causally improve performance in a texture-discrimination task.
records.evidence: Two-photon imaging separated stimulus- and decision-related cells; targeted photostimulation of the decision-coding population improved behavioral choices.
records.boundary: The result is task- and circuit-specific. It does not imply that primary sensory cortex always generates decisions or that every choice-correlated cell is causal.
records.contribution: Moves from correlation to targeted ensemble causality in a defined behavioral setting.

records.title: A modular architecture for organizing, processing and sharing neurophysiology data
records.claim: Modular tools can link neurophysiology files, metadata, laboratory notes, shared storage, programmatic access and automatic analysis across one lab or a multi-lab collaboration.
records.evidence: The paper describes interoperable database, aggregation, access and pipeline modules developed for the International Brain Laboratory.
records.boundary: This is shared infrastructure. It should not be read as evidence for a particular neural computation or as a lab-specific scientific discovery.
records.contribution: Makes the provenance and reproducibility needed for brain-wide collaboration operational.

records.title: Cortico-cortical feedback engages active dendrites in visual cortex
records.claim: Spatially offset feedback from higher visual cortex is nonlinearly integrated in apical tuft dendrites of V1 pyramidal neurons.
records.evidence: Feedback from matched retinotopic locations was relatively suppressive, while offset feedback facilitated responses and generated branch-specific, regenerative-like calcium events in apical tufts.
records.boundary: The experiment identifies one circuit use of active dendrites. It does not show that all cortical feedback, prediction or contextual integration uses this mechanism.
records.contribution: Provides the clearest empirical bridge between dendritic nonlinear computation and natural cortical feedback.

records.title: The influence of cortical activity on perception depends on behavioral state and sensory context
records.claim: The perceptual effect of activating co-tuned V1 neurons changes with sensory contrast and behavioral engagement.
records.evidence: Targeted layer 2/3 photostimulation enhanced low-contrast detection but suppressed high-contrast detection in highly engaged mice; reliable effects were absent when engagement was lower.
records.boundary: The sign and presence of the effect are conditional. The paper does not support a context-free claim that more activity improves perception.
records.contribution: Shows why causal perturbation needs explicit state and stimulus matching.

records.title: A latent pool of neurons silenced by sensory-evoked inhibition can be recruited to enhance perception
records.claim: Sensory-evoked inhibition keeps many non-coding barrel-cortex neurons silent, yet recruiting this latent pool can bias and enhance tactile perception.
records.evidence: Two-photon imaging and patterned photostimulation during whisker discrimination showed preferential inhibitory suppression of non-coding cells and a relationship between their recruitment and perceptual bias.
records.boundary: The result is scoped to the tested barrel-cortex task and targeted populations. It does not mean that silent neurons are generally beneficial to activate.
records.contribution: Recasts sparse non-coding cells as a conditional causal reserve shaped by local inhibition.

records.title: A deep learning strategy to identify cell types across species from high-density extracellular recordings
records.claim: A semi-supervised model trained on curated extracellular waveforms can identify selected neuronal cell types and transfer across probes, laboratories, regions and species.
records.evidence: Ground-truth optogenetic and pharmacological labels in cerebellar recordings supported a classifier exceeding 95% performance in its benchmark, followed by cross-dataset transfer tests.
records.boundary: Performance is tied to represented cell classes, ground truth and acquisition domains. It is not a universal cell-identity oracle.
records.contribution: Adds cell-type resolution to large-scale electrophysiology, including cerebellar learning experiments.

records.title: A brain-wide map of neural activity during complex behaviour
records.claim: Standardized multi-lab Neuropixels recordings reveal how sensory, motor and decision-related activity is distributed across the mouse brain during a common task.
records.evidence: The consortium combined a shared behavioral protocol, anatomically registered recordings and harmonized analysis across laboratories and brain regions.
records.boundary: This is a consortium-level descriptive map. It does not establish that one local cellular mechanism generates the distributed signals.
records.contribution: Provides a common coordinate system for locating local circuit claims inside brain-wide activity.

records.title: Brain-wide representations of prior information in mouse decision-making
records.claim: Subjective prior information is represented across a broad set of regions rather than in a single decision area.
records.evidence: Standardized electrophysiology and widefield imaging found prior-related signals in at least 20-30% of examined regions, spanning early sensory, motor and higher cortical systems.
records.boundary: Distributed encoding is not the same as a proven distributed causal algorithm, and the study does not identify a dendritic implementation.
records.contribution: Shows the spatial scale that mechanistic accounts of prior-guided choice ultimately need to explain.

records.title: A real-time all-optical interface for dynamic perturbation of neural activity during behavior
records.claim: Online calcium analysis, hologram generation and experiment control can be integrated for activity-guided neural perturbation during ongoing behavior.
records.evidence: Proof-of-principle demonstrations detected and recruited neurons online, triggered rapid photoinhibition and delivered activity-guided stimulation during decisions.
records.boundary: The system demonstrates real-time feasibility in selected experiments. It is not yet a general autonomous brain-computer interface or a guarantee of artifact-free closed-loop inference.
records.contribution: Moves all-optical interrogation from preselected targets to state-dependent online control.

records.title: All-optical voltage interrogation for probing synaptic plasticity in vivo
records.claim: Two-photon voltage imaging can resolve subthreshold and suprathreshold dendritic signals while defined cerebellar inputs are optically activated in vivo.
records.evidence: JEDI-2Psub recorded Purkinje dendrite voltage during granule- and climbing-fiber activation; pairing granule-cell input with sensory-evoked climbing-fiber signals induced long-term plasticity in inhibitory responses.
records.boundary: This is a targeted cerebellar demonstration with a specific indicator and preparation, not a universal assay for every synapse or brain region.
records.contribution: Extends causal optical work below calcium events to the voltage signals where synaptic integration and plasticity occur.

records.title: Ultra-high-density Neuropixels probes improve detection and identification in neuronal recordings
records.claim: Much denser recording sites increase neural yield and expose spatial waveform features useful for distinguishing compartments and selected cell types.
records.evidence: NP Ultra more than doubled yield in mouse visual cortex, resolved axonal and dendritic footprints, and improved discrimination among genetically identified cortical interneuron classes.
records.boundary: The denser probe trades recording span for local spatial resolution; reported classification performance is tied to the tested regions, labels and waveform features.
records.contribution: Improves what extracellular recording can observe about cellular identity and subcellular signal origin.

records.title: Fast and slow learning mediated by distinct climbing fiber signals
records.claim: Climbing-fiber signals associated with slow acquisition and rapid remapping differ in content and anatomical organization.
records.evidence: Longitudinal two-photon imaging across cerebellar lobules tracked visuomotor learning and rapid remapping: movement-predictive and reward-related signals changed differently with expertise and reward availability.
records.boundary: This is a preprint and has not completed peer review. Distinct population dynamics do not alone prove fully separate molecular learning rules.
records.contribution: Adds temporal heterogeneity to the cerebellar teaching-signal framework.

records.title: Computational optimization of two-photon holographic stimulation sites in vivo
records.claim: Adaptive optimization can identify holographic stimulation sites that recruit intended targets while reducing off-target activation in vivo.
records.evidence: Non-negative basis-function regression sampled spatial sensitivity and optimized targets in simulations and mouse hippocampal experiments at speeds compatible with closed-loop use.
records.boundary: The optimizer reduces measured off-target effects under tested conditions; it does not eliminate all optical, thermal or network-mediated confounds.
records.contribution: Adds a calibration layer between nominal optical targeting and actual causal specificity.

records.title: Neuropixels Opto: combining high-resolution electrophysiology and optogenetics
records.claim: A single probe can combine high-density extracellular recording with spatially addressable dual-color optogenetic stimulation across cortical depth and deep structures.
records.evidence: Prototype probes integrated 960 recording sites with two sets of 14 emitters, enabling localized activation or silencing and two-color optotagging in mouse brain.
records.boundary: This is a prototype platform with current constraints on emitter use, optical coupling and form factor; broad adoption and long-term reliability remain future questions.
records.contribution: Joins the electrical and optical measurement branches in one spatially addressable device.

takeaways.title: The core is a bridge, not a grand unification
takeaways.body: The most defensible central story connects local dendritic learning, in vivo feedback integration and causal optical interrogation. Cerebellar and brain-wide work expand the program without proving that the same mechanism explains every scale.

takeaways.title: Causal effects are conditional
takeaways.body: The perception studies repeatedly show that a perturbation cannot be interpreted without cell identity, inhibitory context, stimulus strength and engagement state.

takeaways.title: Tools are part of the scientific argument
takeaways.body: Protocol, real-time targeting, voltage readout and off-target optimization progressively close gaps between the intended intervention and the biological event actually measured.

takeaways.title: Consortium work must keep its provenance
takeaways.body: IBL and Neuropixels records are scientifically important, but the atlas labels them as collaborative infrastructure and population-scale evidence rather than silently absorbing them into a lab-owned narrative.

method.inclusion: Selected records dated from 2021-08-09 through 2026-08-09 that clarify a coherent research line, a decisive method transition or a major collaboration layer.
method.exclusion: Corrections, duplicate preprint and version-of-record entries, peripheral co-authorships that do not clarify the map, and publications outside the exact rolling window.
method.claim_rule: Every card separates the paper's scoped claim, the evidence used, and a non-claim or boundary. Reviews and preprints receive distinct status labels.
method.role_rule: Lab-led, review, consortium and multi-lab tool records are shown separately. Authorship order is not used as a substitute for contribution statements.
